name: California State University Long Beach
overview: California State University is the most important public higher education system in the United States. It has 23 campuses, has 450,000 students, 47,000 teachers and employees. The university offers 1,800 Bachelors and Masters in 240 subjects.
administrative:
1. Application Dossier

You will work directly with the partner university regarding your application. All required documents will have to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline (see the Americas Teams channel for each application deadline). If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet. Please be patient.


In the past, the partner has asked for the following:

  • Photocopy of passport / Residence permit (valid more than 6 months after return)
  • Registration forms for ALI and SA@B programs (provided once the destination has been validated by the jury)
  • A letter from the bank with a provision of $13,650 (deferred start) or $20,000 (full year) dated less than 6 months
  • If the bank letter is from a parent's bank account, it must attest to the relationship and mention that the amount available may be used for your expenses during your year abroad in the United States.
  • Course selection form for SA@B (spring) (provided once the destination has been validated by the jury)
  • University insurance subscription consent form (provided once the destination has been validated by the jury)
  • Cover letter in English of at least 250 words explaining why studying at CSULB is relevant to your academic course and your career plans (no recipient in particular, only for CSULB in general)

This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


To be given to Epitech bachelor campus administration to reenroll for the Tech4 (in April/May):

  • The addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier


2. Visa (more information here)

You can find all the detailed information on the US government website or the Embassy of the US in Paris website.


1. Admission letter and I-20 form

When you have been admitted to the university, you will receive an acceptance letter and an I-20 form, allowing you to apply for the F-1 student visa at the embassy. Please check the information on I-20 carefully and sign the document.


2.     Pay the SEVIS fees

 You must then pay the SEVIS I-901 fees online (here). Make sure you print the receipts. The fees for students are $350.


3.     Complete the DS-160 form

Complete DS-160 form and upload an ID photo meeting the following requirements. Print the application form confirmation page to bring to your interview.

You will have to pay a visa application fee (non refundable) before your interview of $185 (more information here).


4.     Schedule an appointment at the consulate

For people in France, you need to make an appointment for your interview at the US Consulate. Plan to travel to Paris for it.

If you live in another country, check the different consulate/embassy.


You can check the deadlines for obtaining an appointment for submitting a file, here.


During your interview at the consulate, you must:

  • have the necessary supporting documents to prove that you qualify for the category of visa that you request--document relating to your current studies and its relationship to the studies you wish to pursue in the United States: academic transcript, various certificates, SAT or TOEFL test scores, diplomas, etc.
  • demonstrate, with supporting evidence, to the consular officer that you have solid family, social and financial ties to France and that you intend to return there once your residence permit has expired.
  • prove that you have the financial means necessary to finance your studies and live in good conditions in the United States for the first 12 months. Any document proving your family or relational ties with any person funding your studies, as well as bank statements, tax notices thereof.

Please note that the visa gives you the right to work 20 hours on campus.


3.Insurance and Health (more information here)

CSULB requires students to purchase their compulsory insurance.

Please check the coverage of the insurance.

On campus, there is a medical center for non-emergency cases.

If you are off campus or cannot wait, check the JCB / Anthem partner doctors/hospitals for affordable rates.

Be aware of “copay” or “coinsurance” amounts that remain your responsibility.


To be fully covered abroad, we recommend all students take out international insurance during their Tech 4. It is imperative that you take out an international insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information. 


In addition, CSULB requires proof of vaccinations prior to course registration (more information here). CSULB will assist if you have questions.

If you cannot get vaccinated or provide proof before departure, vaccines can be administered upon arrival at the CSULB Student Health Center.


If vaccinated in France, bring a copy of your health book. All documentation must be in English.

For more information, you can consult the country's health file a: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/etats-unis.


Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside of France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html


4.Prepare your arrival

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on the US, click here.


5.Campus Life

The campus offers many activities that help students meet others.

Car Rental: avoid renting from Dollar. Recommended: Alamo (professional), Turo (individuals). Always purchase DMV insurance.

In California, you can drive with your French license for 30 days after arrival.

After 30 days, you must obtain the California driving permit. Your I-94 and/or passport stamp are used as proof of entry.

Driving beyond 30 days without a U.S. license is a serious offense, which can lead to: court appearance, high fines, and potential prison/community service (especially in case of an accident)

courses:
Credits

Full Academic Year: you need to earn 24 local credits (12 per semester)

Epitech will cover CSU Long Beach tuition up to the required credits for your program. Any additional courses are your responsibility.


Academic calendar

Fall semester: mid August to mid December

Spring semester: mid January to mid May (includes orientation)


Department and Courses

The Long Beach Full-Year Program - Study Abroad @ the Beach (Semester 1 and 2)

  • 4 classes, each worth 3 local credits
  • Students may take courses in the Computer Engineering and Computer Science department (Level 300/400)
  • Students must send a list of 10 classes that interest them with their application for CSULB. CSULB uses this to plan course offerings.
  • Registration at Long Beach is complex—follow procedures carefully and have backup courses.


In addition to computer courses, you may take classes in:

  • Business
  • Marketing
  • Management
  • Communication
  • Information System
  • Economics


Course Descriptions:

  • CECS (Computer Engineering and Computer Science), level 300 and 400:
  • (EXLUDES ECS 519 "Theory of Computation" & CECS 278 "Cyber Security Principles")

Other courses validated by Epitech (business / management ...) Full course catalogue: http://catalog.csulb.edu/index.php?catoid=5


Please note that physical education classes are not validated.


Important Notes

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits). Part of the requirement to continue to the Spring semester is obtaining a minimum 2.0 GPA or "C" average from the Fall semester
  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.
  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year.
  • If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
  • Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance it.
cost:
Financial Overview (4th Year EPITECH)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the application fees and part of the tuition fees. Epitech will pay the tuition fees at CSU Long Beach to the extent of the credits required according to the program followed. Any additional module will be at your expense.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).


Other Expenses

  • Roundtrip flights: 900 euros / you can also find tickets under 500$
  • Insurance: around $700 per semester and 300-600€ for an additional international insurance depending on the company & the coverage
  • Visa: about 500€
  • Books: 200–370$ per semester *. (from 170 to 320 euros). Please note : you will be invited to buy these books at the Campus bookstore. You should be warned that you can often find cheaper elsewhere.


Estimated Budget

The local currency is the Dollar. 1 € = 1.16USD (rate as of October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.
